study: Fixed-configuration expanded validation of support proposal policies
status: Development validation; not final held-out evaluation
pilot_comparison_scope: The 100-query lists are resampled at the same seeds, not prefixes or strict extensions of the 20-query lists. Corresponding checkpoints and split hashes match. Overlapping queries are not independent evidence.
outcome_definition: A win improves at least one binary necessity/sufficiency metric without worsening the other; loss is the converse. Ties do not imply equal supports or continuous scores.
limitations: Query-budget pairs share queries, graphs and checkpoints; these counts are not independent trials or a significance test.
Only two graphs and two training seeds per graph were evaluated.
The per-step cap is matched, but adaptive stopping changes total proposal counts; gradients and serial checks are additional work.
GPU timings were collected alongside concurrent experiments and other shared-device workloads; they are not controlled speed benchmarks.
The runs use corrected training checkpoints and validation queries; no new held-out test evaluation was performed.
These comparisons omit strong-baseline retuning and do not establish state-of-the-art performance.
Audit checks saved records rather than independently replaying every intervention.
decision: Preserve the single-edge default and all experimental variants. Small, mixed grouping benefits do not yet justify a strong independent-coarsening claim. Do not add more exchange variants solely to optimize these validation lists. Investigate exact local evaluation as a separate computational improvement, with full-graph equivalence checks before integration.
